summary: Egon Wellesz studied at the University of Vienna (~1904–1908). He later held posts at the University of Vienna (~1913–1938) and as a lecturer at the University of Oxford (1943).

Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Eido Shimano studied under Kengan Goto, Keizan Shirozou, and Soen Nakagawa at Ryutaku-ji (1954), and attended the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1960). He founded and led New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

Eiichi Imoto studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1956). Working in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies, he held positions at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1993) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1993–2000).

A scholar of philosophy, Eiichi Makino studied at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903) and taught there (~1903–1938). He also held posts at Kyushu University, Tohoku University, Chuo University, and Shiraume Gakuen Junior College.
Active in religious and Buddhist studies, Eiichi Otani studied at Toyo University (~1987–1996). Around 2018, he served as professor and dean at Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Eiichi Yamaguchi, who works in Indology and philosophy, was a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and subsequently served there as a research assistant (attested 1990–1991).
Working in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history and archaeology, Eiju Fukushima is attested in 2026 as a faculty member at Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.
Eikan Taki, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, was a member of Taisho University and served as a lecturer at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute (attested 2006).

Eiki Hoshino, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Taisho University (~1962–1971). He served at Taisho University (~1980–2013) as a professor in the Faculty of Humanities and as director.
Eiko Okukaze, a Buddhist studies scholar, was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010) and is attested as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University in 2026.

Eileen M. Dimes studied at the University of London (B.A., by 1932). Working in Indology, she was on the library staff at SOAS (1945) and became Assistant Keeper for Modern Indian languages at the India Office Records in 1959.

Historian Eileen Power studied at Oxford High School, Girton College, Cambridge (~1907–1910), and the University of Paris (~1910–1911). She held posts at the London School of Economics (~1921–1940) and the University of London (~1931–1940).

Eilhard Mitscherlich studied at Heidelberg, Paris (under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy), Göttingen, Berlin, and Stockholm. He held posts at the Frederick William University Berlin (~1821–1863) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1822).

Eino Wälikangas studied at the University of Helsinki (~1907–1914; doctoral research under J. N. Reuter ~1910–1917). Specializing in Indology and linguistics, he taught Sanskrit at the University of Helsinki (~1920–1928).

Eisaku Okada studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (2015). In Buddhist studies, he has also held posts at JSPS (2014) and Koyasan University (attested 2014, 2026).
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Eisei Kojima is attested in 1976 as holding posts as a professor at Ryukoku University and as president of Doho University.
Active in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Eishu Miyazaki studied at Rissho University (~1933–1937) and under Gyoo Kageyama. He held posts at Rissho University (~1948–1984) and Minobusan University.
Eishun Fushimi, working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.

Eivind Kahrs studied under Nils Simonsson in the fields of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held a post at Queens' College (attested 2010) and has served as a Council member of the Pali Text Society (attested 2026).
Eiyin Yasuda, who works in Buddhist studies, studied under Gyōin Hashimoto around 1950 and completed studies at Ryukoku University (~1957–1961).
